To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the efficiencies for the 1–3, 1–4 and 1–5 transitions in a Stern—Gerlakh source with a medium field transition and a resonant strong field transition unit are 90.0 ± 0.2, 90.2 ± 0.4, and 90.1 ± 0.3%, respectively.

we designed and built two high-frequency transition units that are capable of producing a polarized deuterion beam with the highest possible figure of merit, that the performance of the units is well understood and that we demonstrated the performance in a realistic internal beam target environment.
we have developed high frequency transition units that allow for the production of polarized deuterons in the internal target of a polarized ion source.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high-frequency transition systems for vector and tensor polarization of atomic deuterium.

the design and construction of a high-frequency transition unit that will be used for the production of polarized deuterons in the internal target of the CEBAF Large Acceptance Spectrometer (CLAS) at Jefferson Laboratory.

the design, construction, testing, and optimization of radio-frequency transition units for the production of high-quality polarized deuterons for use as internal targets in high-energy nuclear physics experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transition efficiencies are in general very high.
the high-frequency transition unit is a robust and reliable tool to produce polarized deuterons.
the design and construction of the high-frequency units were successful and that the units are ready for operation in the polarized internal target experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high-frequency transition technique is an efficient way for producing polarized deuterons for nuclear physics research.
the high-frequency transition unit has proven to be an efficient tool to produce vector and/or tensor polarized atomic hydrogen and deuterium beams for internal target experiments.
the high-frequency transition technique is a very powerful method for the production of polarized atomic beams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transition efficiency of the strong field unit is not limited by the cavity Q factor.

the efficiency of the strong field transition unit is very sensitive to the position of the beam within the cavity structure and that the transition efficiency can be improved by a factor of 10 by optimizing the position of the cavity structure.
high efficiency transition units are feasible, and the design principles developed here will be of great use in the design of transition units for polarizing other atomic and molecular species.
